description: Does a sparingly soluble salt precipitate in this solution (Q vs Ksp), and if it does — or if you add the solid in excess — the equilibrium: how much dissolves or precipitates and the final pH, with the basicity of the anion and the common ion taken into account; next to it the textbook formula, which ignores the pH (the CaCO₃ lesson). Every constant comes with the paper or critical compilation it was taken from.

components.description: What is already in the beaker; empty = pure water

substance.description: A table id ("acetico", "fosforico"), the formula of one of its forms as sold ("NaH2PO4", "NH4Cl", "NH3") or a strong one ("HCl", "NaOH", "AgNO3")

solidInExcess.description: Add the solid salt in excess (saturate) instead of only checking whether it precipitates

name: chem_solubility
